keyVerseText: Jehoahaz was twenty and three years old when he began to reign; and he reigned three months in Jerusalem. And his mother's name was Hamutal, the daughter of Jeremiah of Libnah.
rootMeaning: The name יִרְמְיָה (Yirmᵉyâh) derives from the Hebrew root רוּם (rûwm), which means to lift up, exalt, or rise, combined with the divine element יָהּ (Yah), a shortened form of Jehovah. Thus, the literal meaning of Yirmᵉyâh is "Jehovah will exalt" or "whom Jehovah has appointed." This root sense enriches the common English gloss "Jeremiah" by emphasizing God's active role in raising or appointing the individual, underscoring divine sovereignty and purpose in the bearer’s identity.
usageInScripture: The word יִרְמְיָה occurs 147 times in Scripture, predominantly translated as "Jeremiah" (45 occurrences) and often in relational phrases such as "of Jeremiah" or "unto Jeremiah." This consistent use highlights the prominence of the prophet Jeremiah, son of Hilkiah, as a central biblical figure. Additionally, the name identifies several other individuals, including a father of Hamutal and warriors in David’s time, showing its use as a personal name among Israelites. The range of translations reflects the name's function as both a proper noun and a marker of divine appointment.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding יִרְמְיָה as "whom Jehovah has appointed" reveals the theological truth that God sovereignly calls and elevates individuals for His purposes. Jeremiah, as the major prophet bearing this name, embodies the divine commissioning to proclaim God's word even amid hardship. This divine appointment underscores the faithfulness of God in raising leaders who guide His people according to His will. For Christian faith, it reminds believers that God’s calling is purposeful and that He exalts those who serve Him, pointing ultimately to Christ as the appointed one exalted by the Father.
keyVerseReflection: In 2 Kings 23:31, the name Jeremiah identifies the father of Hamutal, mother of King Jehoahaz, anchoring a personal and historical connection to the prophet’s lineage. The verse states, "Jehoahaz was twenty and three years old when he began to reign... And his mother's name was Hamutal, the daughter of Jeremiah of Libnah." Here, the name Jeremiah conveys not only a familial identity but also a link to a figure appointed by God, emphasizing the providential background of Judah’s royal line. This enriches our understanding of the king’s heritage as connected to one whose name means God’s exaltation.
